<!-- pr-reviewer: d214ef359f02fde5f65cc051e18c17f1edc5b6a1 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a DELTA review of the merge of `origin/main` (`aef12fea6`) into the branch. It reviews the hand resolution of the three conflict files in `295f8b3e9` (3 files, 3 insertions, 14 deletions). The merge of main on top (`d214ef359`) has an empty remerge-diff. It brings only post-merge skip scripts and a one-line `lead_arc_radius: None` test-struct fix. Nothing in that merge touches the review area. The `merge-ready` label and the earlier reviews at `ae4d444e8` and `295f8b3e9` do not count for this head. The base review at the older head is on record. This review does not re-verify unchanged code.

## What looks good

- `pick_kinds.rs:304-308` keeps all three refusal arms. It uses main's fallback: `_ => self.hole_order().err()`. For a kind that is not Drill, Bore or Thread, `hole_order()` returns `Ok(None)`, so `.err()` is `None`. This keeps the old `_ => None` behaviour. No refusal is lost. The sinker refusals stay on the sinker arms. The hole-order refusal stays on the fallback for the hole kinds.
- `mcp/tools.rs:400` keeps the wire, sinker and hole clauses in one sentence. Each clause keeps its own meaning.
- `op_page.rs:169-173` calls `sinker_pick_groups` and `hole_order_groups`. They share one `let u = state.units();`. Both families keep their rows on the Geometry tab.
- `KindInfo::pick()` keeps both arms: sinker Ring/Ends and the hole HoleOrder arm. The capability test covers both families (`start_exit_shared.rs:80,88-89`).
- The three files are unchanged by the outer merge. `git diff 83d52ef6a aef12fea6 -- <the three files>` is empty.

## Results, merged with main (`aef12fea6`)

Runner: self-hosted `camcraft-pr-test`. Run: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/45696449373 (head `d214ef359`, main `aef12fea6`, trial merge clean).

- Quick gate, on the merged tree: GREEN. `wall 18.1 min, 62 step(s), 0 failed, 0 stalled`. This includes `start_exit_shared` (29s), the `sinker_*` suites, `mcp_wire_contour`, `mcp_pick`, `wire_post`, `example_catalog` (28s) and the `camcraft-ui` lib (81s). This matches the coordinator's green 62-step claim.
- Clippy, on the runner: FAILED. The runner has no `cargo-clippy` for its toolchain. The run never reached a lint. The exact error:

```
error: 'cargo-clippy' is not installed for the toolchain 'stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'.
help: run `rustup component add clippy` to install it
```

I re-ran the same clippy locally on the identical tree (`d214ef359`; `origin/main` is an ancestor of this head and the trial merge was a no-op). The command: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Result: exit 0, 0 warnings, 2m12s.
- No conflicts with main: the trial merge was a no-op (`Already up to date`). The PR is `MERGEABLE`.

## Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath change in this delta. The quick plan ran `example_catalog` and its siblings anyway (28s, ok). Nothing was regenerated.
- Light lane: not run. This is a DELTA merge review. The delta reaches no heavy lane. The base review at `ae4d444e8` stands for the unchanged code. The quick gate above is the verification of the touched suites. The runner quick gate was the one review build; `cargo xtask gate light` was not re-run to keep the host at one review build, per the maintainer's note.
- No `P1` under the safety floor: the delta is a conflict resolution that keeps both sides. It changes no output and adds no behaviour. No targeted heavy step.
- No new tests, no golden changes, no snapshot changes. No process files touched.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The schema sentence of `s_edit_op` (`tools.rs:400`) prints the `ring` list (Contour, 5-Axis Contour, Sinker Burn). Its parenthetical also explains Wire Contour, Sinker Side Burn and the hole kinds. The parenthetical mirrors main's existing loose pattern. Main printed the wire and hole clauses the same way. Nothing was copied from or lost against either side.
- The MCP doors pin `the_mcp_doors_name_the_pick_fields_and_the_kinds_that_take_them` (`start_exit_shared.rs:154`) asserts only `picks`, `2D Contour` and `list_operation_types` in the description, and `start_exit` in `list_operation_types`. It does not pin the sinker and hole clauses of the merged description. Consider a pin for those two clauses when the next unrelated change touches that test. Not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
